intro: Look up at Galata Tower, a monument in İstanbul province dating from 1348. The Genoese raised it at the highest point of their Galata walls. For centuries it served as a fire watchtower, and today it is known for the view down over the Golden Horn.
history: The Genoese were granted their colony at Galata by Byzantium, and in 1348 they crowned its walls with this tower, calling it the Tower of Christ. Under the Ottomans it took on many roles: prison, observatory and fire watchtower. Fires and earthquakes changed its cap several times; the cone you see today dates from a twentieth-century restoration.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the conical cap and the viewing gallery. Look for the remains of the Genoese walls, and for the stone shaft of the tower itself.
facts: Did you know? The tower's best known story is also its least verifiable: Evliya Çelebi tells how Hezârfen Ahmed Çelebi strapped on wings and glided from this tower to Üsküdar. The Genoese raised the tower in 1348 at the highest point of their own walls and named it the Tower of Christ. Under the Ottomans it was a fire watchtower, and in a city of timber, the alarm was raised from here.
outro: This brings our tour of Galata Tower to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This tower has watched over the city for centuries; let it keep watching for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
